ordered_targets.name: readHeaders() allows oversized header sections (up to 10240 bytes instead of ≤512)
ordered_targets.mechanism:
readHeaders() accumulates bytes in a ByteArrayOutputStream until it finds the 

 header terminator or reaches HEADER_PART_SIZE_MAX (10240). The library's hardcoded limit (10240) is 20× the application-expected limit (512). Additionally, the linear state machine for 

 detection resets to state 0 on mismatch without partial-match rollback, causing valid terminators to be missed when preceded by partial matches (
 + non-
 byte), extending headers past where they should end.
ordered_targets.resource: CPU time and heap memory: ByteArrayOutputStream in readHeaders() accumulates up to 10240 bytes per header section instead of stopping at the expected ≤512 bytes; each byte is processed individually by readByte() and accumulated into a String
ordered_targets.scale: Measured CPU growth: ~2.8 µs per header byte (linear). At maximum header size within input limit (~10226 bytes in a 10240-byte input), extrapolated CPU ≈ 38 ms, far below the 20s timeout. Allocation grows at ~60 bytes per header byte; at max ≈ 1.3 MB, far below 1 GB heap. Neither timeout nor OOM is reachable. The failure is the harness oracle: readHeaders() returns a header of > 512 bytes (up to HEADER_PART_SIZE_MAX = 10240), the fuzz test throws AssertionError (undeclared throwable). Any input producing > 512 header bytes triggers it; minimum is 513 header bytes in a 527-byte input (1 byte boundary line + 5 byte delimiter + 509 bytes content + 4 byte CRLFCRLF + 7 byte close delimiter). Encoding is 1:1 — each input byte beyond the 14-byte framing becomes one header byte.
